A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SToP research, with matching authors, methods, experiments, and Appendices A–F. All 24 pages in each version were readable, and text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and the appendices, including results in Tables 1–8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and the FlashVid, Argus, and Qwen2.5-VL evaluations in the appendices.

M1.justification: The sink-score definition, STSP attention penalty, and STTP temporal-pruning procedure remain unchanged in Section 4 and Equations 4–6. The revised hyperparameter values concern reported experimental settings rather than a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same coverage: EventHallusion, VideoComp's ActivityNet and YouCook2 domains, VCG-Bench, five MCQA benchmarks, and Argus. The appendix evaluations were already present in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the corresponding experiments, including vanilla models, PruneVid, Holitom, FastVid, VisionZip, FlashVid, hard pruning, attention redistribution, and feature-based pruning.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated μs setting from 0.3 to 0.03 for VisionZip and from 0.2 to 0.02 for FastVid. These are limited revisions to previously reported settings; unchanged results do not establish that experiments were rerun. Other protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The temporal-pruning and sink-removal diagnostics, STSP/STTP ablations, frame-count comparisons, naive-method analyses, and appendix sensitivity studies are retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Statistical and uncertainty reporting remains unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative findings are unchanged, including Tables 1–8 and the appendix analyses. The revised hyperparameter sentence is not accompanied by changed result entries.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, including the computational-cost expression, sink-score definition, and pruning rules, are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about sink tokens, SToP's spatial and temporal components, and improved video understanding under aggressive pruning.

C2.justification: Interpretations of sink-token suppression and temporal pruning remain unchanged, as do the appendix explanations and feature-based-pruning limitation in Appendix E. Corrected section references do not alter these interpretations.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 revises the documented μs values to 0.03 for VisionZip and 0.02 for FastVid. The VisionZip value now agrees with the existing optimum in Appendix D.4 and Figure 10(a). Hardware, other implementation details, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The 54 references, related-work discussion in Section 6, and positioning relative to attention-sink and token-pruning research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Four internal references in Sections 3.1, 4.2, 5.2, and 5.3 are corrected from Section 4 to Section 3.3. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; the narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–8 retain identical displays, captions, and placement. Page arrangement is unchanged, apart from incidental prose wrapping around corrected references.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the discrepancy between Section 5.1's VisionZip μs value and the 0.03 optimum already reported in Appendix D.4 and Figure 10(a). Together with four corrected section references, this modestly improves reproducibility and navigation. The scientific methods, evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
